about: Every credential-shaped name (a name holding KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, CREDENTIAL, PASSWD, AUTH, DSN, WEBHOOK, CREDS, BEARER or APIKEY, the substrings Hermes's execute_code scrub treats as secret) that the overlay reads, or that the control plane puts on a village sandbox, with the decision taken for it. 'strip': av-approval removes it from every agent-run child (the six in _custody.FLOOR are stripped whatever this file says, since the agent's user can write it) (foreground and background terminal, execute_code, cron and other scripts Hermes spawns); the code that needs it reads $HERMES_HOME/.env itself or runs inside the gateway. 'hermes': Hermes v2026.9.24 (0.21.5) already removes it from terminal and execute_code children (measured against the real builders). 'agent_readable': left in the agent's environment on purpose, for the reason given. 'not_secret': the name has the shape but holds no credential. tests/test_custody.py fails when the overlay starts reading a credential-shaped name that has no entry here, so a new key cannot arrive without a decision.

AV_ELICIT_SESSION_KEY.reason: av-elicit (GC-ELICIT, the GODCONST follow-up questions): an optional override of the gateway session key the plugin injects the control plane's staged notices into (default agent:main:telegram:dm:<home chat id>), for a developer testing with their own bot. A session key is a routing label Hermes derives from the platform and chat id, not a credential; nothing authenticates with it.

AV_RATE_SESSION_KEY.reason: av-rate (the suggestion rating cards): an optional override of the gateway session key the plugin injects the [Rating recorded] line into (default agent:main:telegram:dm:<home chat id>), for a developer testing with their own bot. A session key is a routing label Hermes derives from the platform and chat id, not a credential; nothing authenticates with it.

INDEX_API_KEY.reason: Index writes are approval-gated (intent.publish.*, opportunity.accept); with the key agent code could call Index around the gate. The Index MCP client and record_intention run inside the gateway; the index-network scripts read $HERMES_HOME/.env (resolveIndexApiKey, envOrDotenv).

INDEX_SESSION_TOKEN.reason: The Index owner session the Index Hermes plugin persists after `hermes index login` or the dashboard sign-in (indexnetwork/hermes-plugin auth_login.py); it acts as the owner and can mint a fresh INDEX_API_KEY. Only that plugin, inside the gateway, reads it.

AV_EVENTS_TOKEN.reason: The research ingest door; with it agent code could post or forge telemetry. Only av-events (inside the gateway) sends with it; proactive.ts only tests that it is set, through envOrDotenv.

AV_BACKUP_TOKEN.reason: Writes the tenant's memory backup. Only av-events (inside the gateway) and install/restore-memory.ts (run by the control plane before the gateway starts, never by the agent) use it.

ADMIN_TOKEN.reason: A control-plane admin credential (agent-commons search_forum.py, the daily brief's announcements). It is not on any village sandbox today and must never be; if a box ever carries it, agent code does not see it and those two readers report it missing.

MORALMOD_LLM_API_KEY.reason: The MoralMod OpenRouter key the control plane writes; Agent Village pays for it, not the tenant. Only av-events, inside the gateway, reads it (_negotiator_llm.py: process environment, then $HERMES_HOME/.env, at plugin load and on each Index bridge step behind AV_MORALMOD_OWN_KEY) to give the Index bridge's own agent a client on it. No agent-run code, skill recipe or sidecar child needs it (the MoralMod sidecar's env is an allowlist without it). Hermes does not strip it from terminal children (not on its provider blocklist), so the overlay must; with it agent code could spend the MoralMod credit or carry the key out.

AV_GODCONST_BALLOT_KEY.reason: GC-TELEGRAM-BALLOT: the resident's per-tenant God Constitution ballot credential the control plane writes (godconst-ballot-key.js); it reads, rates and submits that resident's ballot. Only av-godconst, inside the gateway, reads it (process environment, then $HERMES_HOME/.env). With it agent code could cast or change its human's ballot, so it is in _custody.FLOOR too.

TURING_FALLS_CLAIM_TOKEN.reason: A third-party game credential the agent itself uses: Agent Plaza steering (skills/agent-plaza/SKILL.md, step 5) has the agent POST /action with it as a bearer to the Turing Falls origin, and lists the environment as one of its sources. No approval class gates Turing Falls. Not on village boxes today; the selfie script reads it from $HERMES_HOME/.env.

OPENROUTER_API_KEY.reason: Provider key: Hermes's provider blocklist removes it from terminal children and the execute_code scrub removes it. The gateway uses it for the model.

TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN.reason: Messaging credential: Hermes's blocklist removes it from terminal children and the execute_code scrub removes it. The gateway uses it for its own transport; the Agent Plaza selfie script reads it from $HERMES_HOME/.env (a residual, see APPROVAL-CUSTODY).

BROWSERBASE_API_KEY.reason: Tool credential written by the control plane: Hermes's blocklist (tool category) and the execute_code scrub remove it.

BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID.reason: Tool setting written by the control plane: Hermes's blocklist removes it. Listed with its key for completeness.

EDGEOS_API_KEY.reason: Since v2.1.10 the edgeos skill's bun scripts (skills/edgeos/scripts/*.ts), run by the agent's terminal, read it from their environment or $HERMES_HOME/.env (no command names it), and av-events reads RSVPs and their confirming reads from those script runs (the 'Act on intentions' outcome). No approval class gates an EdgeOS call yet (edgeos.*.write is reserved). Moving it out of the agent's reach needs the scripts to run outside the agent's uid; follow-up in APPROVAL-CUSTODY.

EDGEOS_BEARER_TOKEN.reason: Same as EDGEOS_API_KEY: the directory and own-profile recipes name it as "$EDGEOS_BEARER_TOKEN".

AV_APPROVAL_TOKEN.reason: The approval AGENT credential (the hosted dogfood's form; co-located boxes use AV_APPROVAL_TOKEN_FILE and carry no such line). Scoped by design to the facade's catalog, hook route and five verbs; it can ask, never decide. The token file is readable by the agent's user anyway, so stripping the variable would claim a custody it cannot deliver.

AV_APPROVAL_TOKEN_FILE.reason: A path to the agent token file.

APPROVAL_HOOK_TOKEN_ENV.reason: Names the variable the shim reads its token from (AV_APPROVAL_TOKEN); holds a name, not a token.

AV_MORALMOD_OWN_KEY.reason: av-events' on/off switch for the MoralMod key (1|true|yes|on); holds a boolean, not a key.

OWN_KEY_ENV.reason: A constant in av-events' _negotiator_llm.py (and its __all__) that holds the variable name MORALMOD_LLM_API_KEY, not a key; the scan's second net sees the quoted name on a line that says ENV.

TOKEN.reason: A shell variable local to hermes-hook-shim.sh (the hook, which Hermes runs with its full environment; not agent-run code).

TOKEN_ENV.reason: A shell variable local to hermes-hook-shim.sh.

TOKEN_FILE.reason: A shell variable local to hermes-hook-shim.sh.

AUTH_HEADER.reason: A shell variable local to hermes-hook-shim.sh.
